description: QUADRA combines four complementary skill sets: Aytaj Shakarzade focuses on business analysis and strategic planning; Turkan Karimova on software engineering; Nurlana Sadigli on networking and cybersecurity; and Nargiz Mehdiyeva on AI and machine learning. We bring together analytical thinking, coding, data analysis, and problem-solving to develop practical solutions using NASA’s open data.
summary:
A building may be suitable for today's climate, but what about 2050?

TOMORROWPROOF explores this question by connecting NASA's historical Earth observation data with building assessment.

Using NASA POWER climate records from 2001–2024, we examine how temperature, humidity, and precipitation have changed over time. Users can select a location, explore its climate history, provide building information, and examine an illustrative future climate scenario.

The idea is simple: climate data should not remain a collection of numbers. It should help us ask better questions before we build.

TOMORROWPROOF turns historical environmental patterns into a starting point for thinking about the long-term climate exposure of buildings.
details:
THE PROBLEM WE ARE ADDRESSING

Buildings are designed and evaluated within environmental conditions, but those conditions do not remain constant. A location that seems suitable today may experience different temperature, humidity, and precipitation patterns over the coming decades.

OUR APPROACH

TOMORROWPROOF introduces a different perspective: instead of looking at a building separately from its environment, we connect the two.

The process begins with a location, not a building specification.

• First, users select a geographical location through an interactive map.
• Then, historical climate observations from NASA POWER (2001–2024) are explored.
• Temperature, humidity, and precipitation patterns are examined to identify historical changes.
• Users provide building information to create an initial assessment.
• Finally, an illustrative 2050 scenario helps explore how different environmental conditions could influence the assessment.

WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT?

Most people encounter climate data as charts, maps, and statistics. TOMORROWPROOF gives those observations a practical context: a building, its location, and the environmental conditions it may face.

We are not claiming to predict the exact weather of 2050 or certify building safety. We are creating a way to bring long-term climate considerations into earlier planning decisions.

TECHNOLOGY

NASA POWER API for historical climate data; Python for data processing and analysis; Leaflet and OpenStreetMap for geographical interaction; and web technologies for the assessment interface.

OUR VISION

We want the question behind construction decisions to evolve from "Does this building work today?" to "Have we considered the environment it may face tomorrow?"
